name: Rosalía
label: Columbia
lede: Rosalía won the one flamenco-singing seat at a Barcelona conservatory, then spent a decade refusing to make the same record twice. The latest, Lux, is an orchestral album about saints, sung in 14 languages.

eras.title: From a Camarón recording to the conservatory
eras.text: Rosalía grew up outside Barcelona in a house with no flamenco in it. What she had was a teenage obsession with the singer Camarón de la Isla and, by 2014, a place at a Catalan conservatory.

years.src: Martin Cid Magazine: Rosalía · Wikipedia: Rosalía
years.h: A Barcelona suburb, and no flamenco at home
years.p: Rosalía is born in Sant Cugat del Vallès and raised in Sant Esteve Sesrovires, a Barcelona suburb where her family has no tradition of Andalusian music.
years.xp: What changed it, in her telling, was a recording of the Cádiz singer [[Camarón de la Isla|1f25c419-4084-40bc-9bac-c39f375384c5]]. Martin Cid Magazine puts her at thirteen when she heard it; Wikipedia says fourteen.

years.h: Her first record is Kejaleo's Alaire
years.p: Rosalía has sung with the flamenco group Kejaleo since 2012. The 2013 album is the first release she appears on.

years.src: Martin Cid Magazine: Rosalía · Wikipedia: Los Ángeles (album)
years.h: One seat a year, and she wins it
years.p: Barcelona's ESMUC takes a single flamenco-singing student annually. Rosalía gets the place and studies under José Miguel Vizcaya, known as El Chiqui.
years.xp:
Martin Cid Magazine says Vizcaya's teaching put rigor ahead of enthusiasm, and that the structural knowledge it gave her is what later let her take the form apart on purpose.

She graduates in 2017, with her debut album already recorded.

eras.title: A summer in the studio with Refree
eras.text: Rosalía spends the summer of 2016 in a Barcelona studio with the guitarist and producer Raül Refree. Universal signs her, and the Spanish press hears a major talent.

years.h: A dancehall hook on C. Tangana's 'Antes de morirme'
years.p: Sony Music Spain releases [[C. Tangana|46d3689c-23e6-46f7-8ad6-c12f13ac9dea]]'s single, produced by [[Alizzz|a4238edc-daf9-42ed-917b-dd586f91c269]], with Rosalía singing on it. It sleeps for two years before it becomes a hit.
years.xp: It resurfaces in summer 2018, the same season her own career takes off, helped along by its use in the Netflix series Élite. Wikipedia lists a peak of number 26 on the Spanish chart.

years.cap: Rosalía and Raül Refree at the Parque de la Cuña Verde, Madrid, July 24, 2017
years.h: Raül Refree gets the guitar and the controls
years.p: At Estudios Calamar in Barcelona, he is co-author, producer, guitarist and arranger on what becomes her debut album.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the two met after Refree saw her perform at the Tablao del Carmen. Universal Music signed her in 2016, and the album came out on its Spanish arm.

years.src: Wikipedia: Los Ángeles (album) · Martin Cid Magazine: Rosalía
years.h: Los Ángeles sands the ornament off flamenco
years.p: Alegrías, tangos, fandangos and seguidillas, plus covers of Enrique Morente's 'Aunque es de noche' and Bonnie 'Prince' Billy's 'I See a Darkness'.
years.xp:
Specialist audiences found it first. It won the Premio Ruido, the Spanish music press's best national album award, announced January 17, 2018, and ABC and Rockdelux both named it Spain's album of 2017.

AllMusic called it "the appearance of a major talent".

eras.title: A bad romance, told in chapters, goes worldwide
eras.text: El Mal Querer turns a 13th-century Occitan novel into flamenco-pop, and the singles do the rest. By the end of 2019 she has a Latin Grammy for Album of the Year and a reggaeton hit with J Balvin.

years.src: Wikipedia: Malamente · Martin Cid Magazine: Rosalía
yt: Malamente, live on Later... with Jools Holland
years.h: 'Malamente' is Chapter 1
years.p: The lead single of El Mal Querer comes out May 30, 2018 on Columbia, with a video from the Barcelona production company Canada.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says it was recorded in 2017 at Casa Arte on El Hierro in the Canary Islands. Pitchfork later named it the 23rd best song of the 2010s.

Not everyone in flamenco was sold. Martin Cid Magazine quotes the veteran singer José Mercé saying not everything is valid, and that any small thing is not flamenco.

years.h: One microphone in El Guincho's Barcelona apartment
years.p: [[El Guincho|7e57d8a2-e6eb-48dd-8e50-ff7eaa412ccb]] and Rosalía record El Mal Querer with a computer, an audio interface and that microphone. Rosalía says she was in the red when the album came out.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes the setup and says Rosalía put her own money into what she treated as a university project, with the concept developed alongside her friend Ferran Echegaray.

years.cap: Rosalía with Rosy de Palma and Pedro Almodóvar at Festival Cultura Inquieta, November 21, 2018
years.src: Wikipedia: El Mal Querer · Wikipedia: Rosalía
years.h: El Mal Querer follows one bad relationship, chapter by chapter
years.p: Rosalía and El Guincho produce eleven tracks, each a chapter of the anonymous novel Flamenca. Pitchfork names it the sixth best album of 2018.
years.xp:
Metacritic scored it 89. Pitchfork's Philip Sherburne wrote that hers was "as commanding a presence as Spanish-language pop has encountered in ages". Alexis Petridis gave it five stars in The Guardian.

The singles came in a chain: 'Pienso en tu mirá' in July, 'Di mi nombre' three days before the album, 'Bagdad' in December and 'De aquí no sales' in January 2019.

years.cap: Rosalía on the red carpet at the Goya Awards, Seville, February 2, 2019
years.h: 'Con Altura' becomes 2019's most-watched female video on YouTube
years.p: [[J Balvin|5bdeb32d-56a5-4b6d-a768-264101fa0a0a]] and [[El Guincho|7e57d8a2-e6eb-48dd-8e50-ff7eaa412ccb]] are on the single; Director X shoots the video.
years.xp:
It began in September 2018 in Miami, and its title comes from a phrase by the Dominican influencer Mariachi Budda that the track samples. Wikipedia reports over 1.5 billion streams in 2019.

The video won two MTV VMAs, Best Latin and Best Choreography, making her the first Spanish artist to win at the ceremony. Balvin had put her on his 2018 song 'Brillo' first.

years.cap: Rosalía at Palau Sant Jordi, Barcelona, December 7, 2019, on the El Mal Querer tour
years.src: Rolling Stone: Latin Grammys 2019 · GRAMMY.com: Bad Bunny, Rosalía
yt: Album of the Year acceptance, 2019 Latin Grammys
years.h: Rosalía takes Album of the Year at the Latin Grammys
years.p: At 26 she becomes the second solo woman to win the night's top prize, after Shakira in 2006, and thanks J Balvin from the stage.
years.xp:
Grammy.com quotes her on winning: "I'm serious, I'm in shock. This is the last thing I expected." She also took Best Urban Song for 'Con Altura' and performed a medley that night.

Sources differ on the total: Wikipedia counts six wins for the album, while Grammy.com's recap lists five awards for her.

eras.title: Everybody wants her on the track
eras.text: Between tours she turns up on records by Travis Scott, Bad Bunny, Arca and Billie Eilish, while the next album takes shape in Miami during the pandemic.

years.h: Rosalía becomes the first Spanish woman to perform at the Grammys
years.p: She is also the first Spanish-speaking act nominated for Best New Artist at the 62nd Grammys, and El Mal Querer wins Best Latin Rock, Urban or Alternative Album.

years.h: 'TKN' goes viral on TikTok and lands on the Hot 100
years.p: The May 2020 single with [[Travis Scott|e4a51f17-a57b-47b1-b37b-f552d0f8e9e6]] debuts at number 66, and its video wins a Latin Grammy for Best Short Form Music Video.
years.xp: A month later, on June 22, came 'KLK', her collaboration with the producer [[Arca|f7625f34-1799-42a4-a1c6-22b5377c767b]], on his album KiCk i.

years.h: Bad Bunny's 'La Noche de Anoche' drops on Valentine's Day
years.p: The single from [[Bad Bunny|89aa5ecb-59ad-46f5-b3eb-2d424e941f19]]'s El Último Tour del Mundo features Rosalía and debuts at number two on Spotify's global chart.
years.xp: Wikipedia reports 6.63 million first-day streams, the biggest debut for a Spanish-language song on Spotify at that point.

years.h: The Weeknd joins an experimental bachata called 'La Fama'
years.p: The first single from Motomami, with [[The Weeknd|c8b03190-306c-4120-bb0b-6f2ebfc06ea9]], is her seventh number one in Spain.
years.xp: A month later, in December 2021, Rockstar Games launched a Grand Theft Auto Online radio station called Motomami Los Santos, curated by Rosalía and Arca.

eras.title: Pistons, filters and a new storyline
eras.text: She drops the flamenco plot for experimental reggaeton: hard drums, vocal chops, ballads that curdle. Metacritic calls Motomami the best-reviewed record of 2022, and a runway stage show follows.

years.h: 'Saoko' shoots its video in Kyiv
years.p: The second Motomami single is filmed at Podilskyi Bridge; the video later wins the MTV VMA for Best Editing.

years.h: Pitchfork gives Motomami 8.4 and Best New Music
years.p: Columbia releases it March 18, 2022; Metacritic calls it the best-reviewed album of the year.
years.xp:
The title honors her mother Pilar Tobella, who used to get her around town on a motorcycle; her mother's company, Motomami S.L., was set up in 2018. Rosalía has described the record as split between a strong, experimental Moto side and a personal, confessional Mami side.

It was recorded between March 2020 and August 2021 in Barcelona, New York (including Electric Lady), Los Angeles and Miami, with producers including [[Noah Goldstein|2dad5809-0d9b-40cf-85cf-2f8828ffaaf0]], [[Pharrell Williams|149f91ef-1287-46da-9a8e-87fee02f1471]], [[Tainy|7e92584c-ca97-48bf-8a12-0327db0f6ac8]], Frank Dukes and El Guincho.

years.cap: Rosalía at Movistar Arena, Santiago, Chile, August 28, 2022, on the Motomami World Tour
years.h: The runway tour opens in Almería
years.p: A white cyclorama, two vertical screens and a 20-meter runway; the crew grows from about 40 to over 150. It ends December 18 in Paris.
years.xp: Tour manager Agustín Boffi said the crew expanded to "over 150 people" from 40 on the previous cycle. Dates included Madrid's WiZink Center, London's O2, Radio City Music Hall and Mexico City's Auditorio Nacional; the São Paulo show was moved to a bigger venue.

years.h: 'Despechá' arrives three weeks into the tour
years.p: The song on the Motomami deluxe edition becomes a global hit.
years.xp: Wikipedia describes it as a track that began life in the live show before it was released.

years.h: A second Album of the Year, a first for a woman
years.p: Motomami takes the Latin Grammy, making Rosalía the first woman to win it twice as lead artist. At the Grammys in February 2023 it also won Best Latin Rock or Alternative Album.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Rolling Stone, Pitchfork, The New York Times and W Magazine criticized the Recording Academy for leaving the album out of the main Grammy Album of the Year race.

years.h: She and Rauw Alejandro put out an EP called RR
years.p: [[Rauw Alejandro|197b70c7-8910-4030-ad03-632d82aa40e3]] is the other half. The single 'Beso' becomes a global success.

years.h: Björk revives 'Oral', shelved since 1998, and Rosalía sings it
years.p: [[Björk|87c5dedd-371d-4a53-9f7f-80522fb7f3cb]] wrote the song in 1998 and set it aside as too poppy. She and Rosalía give the income to AEGIS, a group fighting salmon farming in Iceland.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the proceeds go to legal fees for Icelandic activists opposing open net-pen fish farming. The video, directed by Carlota Guerrero, uses AI-generated deepfake versions of both singers.

eras.title: Lux goes orchestral
eras.text: Lux takes three years, the London Symphony Orchestra and lyrics in 14 languages, with saints behind the songs. Metacritic scores it 95, and the arena tour that follows is staged as part opera, part ballet.

years.big: "Maybe I'm writing songs, but I'm not finishing the thought."
q: Why do you have to destroy the song always?
years.src: AOL: How a Fight with Her Sister · HIGHXTAR: Rosalía talks to Apple Music
years.h: Her sister's verdict on Motomami stings, and sticks
years.p: Pili, Rosalía's sister, stylist and creative director, asks the question in a car while they listen to Motomami. Rosalía has said it stung and changed how she wrote.
years.xp:
Ahead of Lux, Rosalía said the remark made her ask whether she was finishing her thoughts, and that answering it let her grow as writer, arranger and producer.

She told Apple Music: "MOTOMAMI was minimalist; this is maximalism. Brutalism."

years.h: 'Berghain' with Björk and Yves Tumor opens the Lux era
years.p: Sung in German, Spanish and English, it debuts at number one in Spain. The video, shot in Warsaw, is directed by Nicolás Méndez of the production company Canada.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Rosalía wrote it with Björk, Yves Tumor and the producers Noah Goldstein, Sir Dylan and Jake Miller. It reached number 22 on the Billboard Global 200, and The Guardian named it one of the 20 best songs of 2025.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lux (Rosalía album) · Soap Central: Pitchfork rates Rosalía's Lux · Fridge Cigarette: A Vibes-Based Review · NPR: On 'Lux,' Rosalía
yt: The Zane Lowe Interview on Lux
years.h: Pitchfork gives Lux 8.6 and Best New Music
years.p: Columbia puts it out with the London Symphony Orchestra. Pitchfork later ranks it No. 16 on its 50 best albums of 2025.
years.xp:
Lux is in four movements, with songs inspired by saints including Hildegard of Bingen, Joan of Arc, Teresa of Ávila and Saint Rosalia of Palermo, and lyrics in 14 languages per Wikipedia (NPR and Apple Music say 13). Daníel Bjarnason conducts the LSO; guests include Björk, Carminho, Estrella Morente, Sílvia Pérez Cruz and Yahritza y su Esencia, and among the producers are Caroline Shaw and Pharrell Williams. It was announced October 20, 2025.

Pitchfork called it "a heartfelt offering of avant-garde classical pop that roars through genre, romance, and religion." Metacritic scores it 95, The Guardian and Rolling Stone gave five stars, and The Guardian and Consequence made it their number one of 2025. Wikipedia reports 42.1 million Spotify streams on day one, a record for a female Spanish-language artist.

years.h: 'La Perla' gives her a 13th number one in Spain
years.p: With Yahritza y su Esencia on the record, Rosalía performs it solo on The Tonight Show, staged after The Princess and the Pea. It becomes the album's second single on December 5.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists number one in Spain and Argentina, number three on Hot Latin Songs and number 12 on the Global 200. The video, directed by Stillz (Matías Vásquez), who also worked on Motomami visuals, came out December 16.

years.h: Rosalía and Björk play 'Berghain' at the Brits
years.p: She also becomes the first Spanish-speaking winner of International Artist of the Year.
years.xp: The performance was accompanied by the Heritage Orchestra. In May 2026 she also won International Songwriter of the Year at the Ivor Novello Awards.

years.cap: Rosalía opening her Lux show at Unipol Forum, Milan, March 2026
years.h: Outside Lyon, the Lux Tour opens with an orchestra
years.p: Fifty-seven shows through September 16, including London's O2 (May 5-6) and Madison Square Garden (June 16-17).
years.xp:
The show runs in four acts and an intermezzo, from ballet and religious imagery to a darker electronic persona, with the Heritage Orchestra, conducted by Yudania Gómez Heredia, on a B-stage laid out as a Latin cross.

Alexis Petridis called it "one of the boldest, most highbrow arena shows in pop history"; Rolling Stone called it "part opera, part ballet, part pop extravaganza".

years.h: Fontaines D.C. put her on 'Where Is Gone?'
years.p: Wikipedia lists her on the track from [[Fontaines D.C.|fd87acc7-e0a0-4a45-bc2a-d2ab5c10be68]]'s album Dopamine Chamber, dated September 17, 2026.
